channel.title: Crypto Daybook
channel.description: Crypto Daybook reports daily crypto news: market moves, Bitcoin and Ethereum updates, exchange and protocol developments, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: Why token decimals matter in cross-chain swaps
item.description: Token decimals turn raw units into readable amounts, and mismatches can make a cross-chain swap look rounded, mispriced or short after a transfer.

item.title: Ledger reviews wallet sales after $90 million hack
item.description: Ledger is reviewing sales and anti-tampering controls after an implant in reseller-sold wallets captured recovery phrases; outside estimates put crypto losses near $90 million.

item.title: One-Step Swaps or Bridge Trades: How to Compare Them
item.description: Compare one-step swaps with bridge trades by tracing each route’s fees, timing, and final token, then choose the path that fits the transfer best.

item.title: Check the Whole Route Before Choosing a Crypto Bridge
item.description: A bridge’s arrival estimate covers only part of a cross-chain transfer. Check exchange withdrawal time, source confirmations and destination steps before choosing.

item.title: When a Token Hook Changes Your Bridge Route
item.description: A token transfer hook can make a bridge transaction fail unless its route supports the required checks and accounts, so compare the destination asset before signing.

item.title: Four checks before choosing another crypto route
item.description: When a crypto withdrawal pauses, check the asset, destination network, route status and total cost before choosing another path or waiting it out.

item.title: What Happens After You Send a Cross-Chain Swap?
item.description: A cross-chain swap is a sequence of deposits, checks and payouts across two blockchains, so the final transfer can take longer than the first. Fees apply at each step.

item.title: Check the token before you send it from your wallet
item.description: Check the token name, network and contract address before sending. These quick steps can help you avoid sending an asset to the wrong place.

item.title: Five Checks for a Token After a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: After a cross-chain swap, match the destination chain, token contract, transaction record and token behavior before relying on the asset in your wallet.

item.title: Check the Token Before a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: Check the token’s chain and contract address before a cross-chain swap; matching names are not proof, and the destination token may have a different address.

item.title: How to reach a lending market on another chain
item.description: A bridge can move tokens toward a lending market, but the destination still needs the right asset, liquidity and a separate supply transaction.

item.title: When a Small Swap Refund Is Pending, Should You Retry?
item.description: A small swap refund can take time to settle; check its transaction status and destination before retrying, since a second attempt may create a second trade.

item.title: Five steps to move bitcoin proceeds into L2 stablecoins
item.description: Moving bitcoin proceeds into an L2 stablecoin takes a route, a destination and enough gas; check each before you send funds or approve a swap.

item.title: Ledger unveils Atom, a secure Android device for crypto users
item.description: Ledger unveiled Atom, a data-connected Android device that pairs everyday apps with hardware-checked crypto approvals as scrutiny over wallet tampering intensifies.

item.title: How to Track Exchange Rates During a Wallet Bridge
item.description: Track a bridge quote from the wallet’s starting token to the amount received, then separate market movement from fees, slippage and route changes before you send.

item.title: Four checks for a pending Mantle bridge transfer
item.description: A pending Mantle bridge transfer can be at different stages. Check the transaction, wallet address, destination balance and withdrawal claim before taking action.

item.title: Turning Sale Proceeds Into a Protocol Stablecoin
item.description: Converting sale proceeds into a protocol stablecoin depends on the token’s chain, route liquidity, fees and the protocol’s accepted asset—not just the quoted price.

item.title: Why Thin Liquidity Can Change a Mantle Exit Route
item.description: When a Mantle withdrawal hits thin liquidity, a provider may route through other pools or assets, trading a faster payout for added fees, slippage and risk.

item.title: How to confirm a cross-chain swap arrived
item.description: A successful send on the source chain is only the first step. Check the destination chain, wallet address and token transfer to confirm the swap arrived.

item.title: Check the Whole Quote Before a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A cross-chain quote is an estimate, not a promise. Compare the amount delivered, fees, route, timing and expiry before approving the wallet transaction.
